responses.text: Wow. That thing is definitely carrying around a bunch of Enclave intel. Adams is on the eastern seaboard of the country.
Which means this little "Duraframe" sucker somehow managed to survive for over {thinking} two thousand miles. {impressed} Certainly lives up to its model name.
I don't want to be... alarmist or anything, but maybe you should ditch that Eyebot. {catching himself} Robot. Whatever that thing is.
Who knows what it's programmed for? Maybe tomorrow you'll take out an iguana-on-a-stick and that'll activate its {searching} mini-nuke self-destruct sequence.
I don't know if you care about my opinion, but I'd prefer that you turn ED-E over to the Followers. Surprised, right?
Easy as a heart transplant.
Okay.
{joking} I thought my charm could win you over, but I guess it wasn't meant to be. Are you sure you want me to go?

topics.prompt: It's time for us to part ways.

responses.text: {"Thought so."} Mmm hm.

topics.prompt: On second thought, stick with me for a little longer.

responses.text: I'll head back to the Old Mormon Fort. If you need me, just swing by.
{sighing} Back to the tomb, I suppose. If you need me, et cetera.

topics.prompt: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.

responses.text: You have quite the menagerie at your disposal. If you can get the posse down to "small gang" size, I'll happily go with you.
As the old saying goes, two's company, but three's a small army. Okay, I'm paraphrasing a bit, but you get the idea.
There's something about that robot that doesn't seem... all right to me. I'm not saying we shouldn't take it with us.
I'm just saying that if it were to "fall" into Lake Mead and be irreparably damaged... and if you threw an EMP grenade in after it...
Well, there are worse things happening in the world, right?
After spending thirty years of my life hiding my association with the Enclave, I'd {emph} love to stroll the wasteland with a twitchy Eyebot.
Back in your good graces again? I knew you'd see the light.
A courier, doctor, and a cybernetic dog. After we deal with the whole "imminent conquest of New Vegas" problem, we should open an act at the Tops.

topics.prompt: I think we should travel together.

responses.text: Lead the way.
{a little annoyed} I'm not exactly in Power Armor over here, so why don't you help lighten my load a bit?
{annoyed} I'm not standing here because I'm overburdened with emotion. Take some of this stuff off of me so I can move a little more easily.
{hushed, not confident in his abilities} O... kay. I'll do my best.
{quietly} Just as a warning, my covert bandaging skills are a little rusty.
I'll defer to your judgment, naturally.
{worried} I'll do my best.

topics.prompt: I want you to change your combat style.

responses.text: Understood. I won't hesitate.

topics.prompt: I want you to attack enemies the moment you see them.

responses.text: Not a problem.
After you.
If you would like me to die very rapidly, this is clearly the best tactical choice.
I'm hardly a whirlwind of death when left to my own devices, but all right.

topics.prompt: I want you not to attack enemies unless I've already engaged them.

responses.text: {sounds great to him} No arguments from me.

topics.prompt: I want you to use ranged weapons.

responses.text: Just tell me where you want me.

topics.prompt: Let's talk about how close you're following me.

responses.text: I'm not going to wander off, but okay.
Okay.

topics.prompt: Your distance is good. Let's talk about something else.

responses.text: Got it.

topics.prompt: All right, you're good. Let's get out of here.

responses.text: Wherever you want me. No problem.

topics.prompt: Keep your distance. Try to flank them.

responses.text: Let me know if you need anything else.
Sure. Just don't treat me like a pack Brahmin, okay?
I'll be here. Just don't expect me to fend off a gang of Super Mutants while you're gone.
Okay. Just don't be gone long. I sunburn easily.
Like I said, I needed to go do something. This is it. It belonged to my father.
Since you convinced me to help out with the defense of Hoover Dam, I figured I'd haul it out of storage.
I'm a little rusty with it but... I think I can manage. {bit of a grin} As long as you've got my back, of course.
Like I said, I needed to go do something. This is it. It belonged to my father.
I thought I might wear it at Hoover Dam, but after you talked me out of it, I didn't see the point in hanging on to it any longer.
I'm here because of you, so I figure you're the one most deserving of it. It should protect you from everything short of a Plasma Caster.
And if you need anything - anything at all - you know where to find me.
{false friendly} Hey there. Was it always your plan to sell me into slavery to Caesar, or was that a spur of the moment thing?
Why don't you make like Odysseus and get lost?
For as lack of adornment is said to become some women, so will this place, without your presence, bring delight.
I've run out of witty ways to tell you to leave, so why don't you just go?
If you want to talk, take off that ridiculous Legion uniform. It's insulting.
Hi. If you're looking for medical help, try the other doctors. I'm just a researcher. Not even a particularly good one.
Hello, again. Still in one piece, I see.
What's up?
Well, we've had some laughs, you and I, but it looks like you're a crazy person and I'm going to have to leave.
Moreno took the fall of the Enclave hard. He never questioned his orders, never questioned the legitimacy of what the Enclave was doing.
To him, it was all one unbroken chain, from Washington to Richardson. When we left Navarro, I remember looking up at Moreno.
He said, "Kiss America goodbye, boys." When we left the Enclave behind, the love in him burned itself out. Now there's just a bitter old man left.
Since my mother died, Daisy's been the only woman in my life. She was the only other woman close to my father, too.
She flew him out on over a dozen missions, including his last. I've always been close to Daisy.
There have been some good men along the way, but lovers make poor confidants. Daisy never had children of her own, so she was always there to listen.
Being in the Enclave didn't mean much to her. She just loved to fly. It broke her heart to be grounded.
Doc Henry always was a hard one to figure out. It didn't seem to matter whether he was working with humans or dogs.
He had an equal lack of affection for both. A regular {dai-ah-jen-eez} Diogenes. I'm not sure what the man was after.
"Knowledge is power," but to what end for Henry, I have no idea. The problem was what mattered to him, not its practical impact.
He simply solved riddles because they existed.
If I had to pick anyone who didn't belong in the Enclave, it would definitely be Johnson. He hated what the Enclave was doing.
Day to day, week to week, he would question orders, subvert mission objectives, do anything he could to serve without serving.
It's amazing he was never court-martialed. He always had good things to say about my father. Said I was like him in a lot of ways. I wish I knew.
Judah Kreger is the glue that's kept us all together over the years, and with good reason.
Anyone who can command Moreno and Johnson in the same unit without somebody getting fragged is one hell of a leader.
Kreger was polite and kind, but never warm. He always did his best to make me feel welcome in the group.
I think he did it out of a sense of loyalty to my father. Loyalty means a lot to Judah.
Not loyalty to the Enclave, or even the ideals they fought for, but to the people who served with him.
I'd like to say that I saw this coming, but honestly I was oblivious. {sheepish} For what it's worth, I'll do what I can to help you... not get killed?
So Mr. House doesn't care that one of Caesar's most notorious Legion spies is walking around on the Strip.
Either that or his Securitrons' AI is too primitive to recognize the threat. Neither answer is particularly comforting.
{sarcastic, in response to being ignored by another Follower} Oh, hello Emily. Yes, it is I, Arcade Gannon, fellow member of the Followers of the Apocalypse.
Would I like to help infiltrate the Lucky 38{casino} ? I'm so glad you asked...
That's a lot of energy weapons. Brings back some interesting memories.
The Strip's not a bad place if you love terrible things and people. {a bit sad, annoyed} I'll never understand the allure of giving away your money to the rich.
I've read about REPCONN. I think they did some work with the... {catching himself, was about to say "Enclave"} the government before the war. Rockets and some energy weapon prototypes, I think.
Westside, huh? I passed through here with another Follower a while back, Anderson. The locals were having a lot of trouble getting water through.
Westside, huh? I heard about what happened with Anderson. Can't say I'm surprised. He was always a fringe operator in the Followers.
{exasperated} What's wrong with you? Killing Anderson isn't going to bring Corporal White back.
Interesting way of handling things. Very {soob} sub {roh-sah} rosa.
I don't know if the Scorpions deserved to be wiped out for something they didn't do, but that's one less problem Westside has to deal with.
Anderson turned in for the wrong reason and Westside gets to keep siphoning water.
It's hard to find justice in all of this, but I suppose this is as close as it gets. Thanks.
Extortion? Really? You go through all of this only to extort the people who are trying to help Westside? Unbelievable.
Hildern is a good example of "big picture" obsession gone too far.
At some point he became so fixated on large scale results that he lost the concept of "the common good" along the way.
It's an inhumane kind of public service when people and the basic resources they need become numbers in a ledger.
A vertibird. Interesting. It's been a long time since I've seen one of these.
Wait, wait, wait a second. What's going on? Am I playing Vergil to your Dante?
I'd like to assume that we're tiptoeing into the mouth of hell out of academic curiosity, but I'm not so open-minded that I've lost my brains.
I guess I'll wait out here, then.
I need to talk to you about something, if you have a minute.
Thanks for doing this, getting them all back together again.
I'll be honest, when Moreno started going off, I didn't think we'd all be walking out of there in one piece.
I still don't know how this is all going to shake out in the end, but at least the Enclave can atone a bit for all the damage it's done.
I shouldn't be surprised at what happened with Moreno. I hoped that after all this time, he could put his anger behind him.
Maybe everything good in Orion Moreno died at Navarro and it was foolish to think there was anything in him left to salvage.
You got the survivors of the Enclave back together so you could convince them to help Caesar?!
What are you thinking? Do you {emph} want to see Vegas turned into the new slave capital of the west?
Hey. You're your own person and all that, but you're acting crazy, and if you keep it up, I'm going to leave.
I like how you handled that. Nicely done.
I can't say that's how {emph.} I would have handled that, but...
You're that courier, right? The guy who runs the Tops, Benny... heard he tried to kill you.
I guess that didn't work out very well for him. {joking} Should I watch my back around you?
Oh, you're that courier, aren't you? The one who got mixed up with Benny over at the Tops. Sounds like messy business.
I'm no botanist, but I think this {emph} may not be entirely natural.
Nuclear waste disposal. Pre-War, people figured there was so much desert in Nevada, you might as well turn it into a big dumping ground.
People didn't like it, but they weren't about to give up easy access to power, not with all of the petroleum drying up.
It's a shame what happened up here. I understand arguments about the "fog of war", but that can't be much consolation to the survivors.
{sadly} Or to the NCR soldiers who have to live with what they did here.
In case it's not obvious, I think you should redirect the power to Freeside and outer Vegas.
You activated ARCHIMEDES?! What the hell are you thinking?!
Nicely done. I'm sure people will appreciate the power. I hate to have to rely on it, but out here... it makes a big difference.
Hmm. I suppose an even distribution is better than nothing.
Everything to the Strip and McCarran? Are you kidding? {sighs}
{irritated} I guess I should be grateful you didn't activate the laser.
You have to hand it to the NCR. Get enough hands working together and they can make or break just about anything.
I'm not exactly a mercenary, but taking out scumbags of this magnitude wouldn't cause me to lose any sleep.
Well, I'll be. Hoover Dam. One of the last remaining {emph} functioning wonders of the Pre-War world.
I'm amazed it's still running at all. Too bad everyone's killing each other over it.
What a load of Brahmin shit! Can you believe that guy?
{irritated that the player is shooting near him} Stop doing that, please.
{annoyed} I'm not sure if you're trying to hit me or trying to miss me. Either way, stop it. Thanks.
{player is aiming gun at Arcade} I assure you, you look extremely virile. Now, would you mind pointing that somewhere else? Thanks.
{player is aiming gun at Arcade} Uh... {cautiously} what's up?
{player is dropping mines near Arcade} Can't wait to see where this is going.
{he just threw a grenade} Look out!
Oh, you know. Finding alternative treatments for common illnesses and injuries. Stimpaks out of barrel cacti and other fantastic improbabilities.
As far as fruitless wastes of time go, it's quite noble in its aims.
Not all Followers are "people persons." Besides, someone needs to do research. I have no problem with Julie sticking me back here.
Out of sight, out of mind. There are worse things one can be, though I do admit, it is a bit boring.
Though it has a noble goal, I don't think this research will yield much fruit. No pun intended.
Like I said before, not all Followers are good with people.
I'm fine doing research back here, even if it is a bit boring... and pointless... and a complete waste of time.
Don't mind me. I'm just voicing my thoughts so they don't burrow out of my skull in a fit of abject despondency.

topics.prompt: Why do you do research instead of providing medical assistance?

responses.text: I'm enthusiastic about helping people, but {nih-hill noh-wee soob soh-lay} nihil novi sub sole.

topics.prompt: You don't sound too enthusiastic about it.

responses.text: For the past hundred years or so, the Followers have managed to get by using salvaged medical supplies from the Old World.
But the side effect of medical success is that more people live longer. Funny how that works.
Eventually, we'll run out of hospitals to loot. We need new ways to produce those supplies. Or maybe old ways, if this research goes anywhere.
Cuts, lacerations, broken bones. Infections resulting from all of the above. Common cold, influenza. Take your pick.
There are plenty of ways to die out here, and most of them, surprisingly, don't have anything to do with war. Just common human fragility.

topics.prompt: What kinds of illnesses and injuries?

responses.text: {“Yeah, well...”}{SEE-zar} Caesar can cite {KAY-toe} Cato to suit his purpose. Many people have spoken Latin. Some of them were quite pleasant.
It's unfortunate that the language is now associated with the gentlemen across the river.

topics.prompt: Isn't that the language that Caesar's Legion speaks?

responses.text: Oh. {sincere} Sorry. "There is nothing new under the sun."
If agave and mesquite were that miraculous, the locals would have figured it out a few thousand years ago.
Not from the Legion, if that's what you're getting at. Books. Sheet music. Gladiator movie holotapes. Bits and pieces here and there.
The Followers have extensive libraries, but we all draw water from the same old well. Even Caesar.
{sighs} I don't know anything that the others couldn't tell you. Caesar was one of the Followers. Before my time, of course.

If you set aside his leadership capabilities, extensive knowledge, and ruthless cunning, he's just another jerk who steps on people to get his way.

topics.prompt: Do you know much about Caesar?

responses.text: I can't leave now. Caesar has gained too much ground. I need to be here in case the NCR fails to hold Hoover Dam.

topics.prompt: Why don't you come with me?

responses.text: {off-hand, not realizing he's revealing something bad} Energy weapons? Of course not.
{catching himself, trying to cover} I mean... but, we study all sorts of science and technology so, you know, we... you just kind of get familiar with them. Yeah.

topics.prompt: Do the Followers use a lot of energy weapons?

responses.text: Oh, uh... {trying to cover} of hearing stories. About energy weapons. {drifting off} They're... pretty crazy. {quietly} Yeah.
Did I say something? Sorry. Don't pay any attention to me. Just babbling. {becoming more quiet} Nonsense, really. {drifting off} Babbling nonsense.
Very optimistic of you. You'll make a good Follower someday assuming Caesar doesn't have us both crucified.

topics.prompt: I just want to hear Caesar out.

responses.text: Short of canceling our imminent travel plans, that's the best thing you could have said.

topics.prompt: Let's just listen to him, figure out what he's up to, and get out.

responses.text: {"And you, my friend?" eht too mee ah-mee-kay?} Et tu, mi amice?
{"And you, my friend?" eht too mee ah-MEE-kah?} Et tu, mi amica?

Just give me a sign when you're about to pull out the dagger so I know when to make a run for the cliffs.

topics.prompt: I'm not going to let Benny get away.

responses.text: The NCR had a chance to use the Followers' skills before, but being imperialists mattered more to them. No thanks.

topics.prompt: I'm trying to help Mr. House keep New Vegas independent.

topics.prompt: The NCR oppression around here would disappear if the Legion took control. I could use your help.

If you plan to help Caesar's Legion, this is going to be a brief relationship.
I may not have all the answers for how to fix Freeside's problems, but Caesar taking control isn't part of the solution. Fair?

topics.prompt: Things are bad around here. I'd like to make a difference, and I'd like you to help me.

responses.text: Hmm. Wow. You sound like you really do need some help. Look, I can help you out, but you can't do anything stu-
I mean, you can't... help bad people, who want to hurt the locals in Freeside. If you do, I'll leave. Does that make sense?

topics.prompt: This place is really complicated and stuff. You're smart. Can you help me do... things?

topics.prompt: Ugh. Well if you're going to be like that then never mind.

responses.text: {slight mockery} Uh... probably not. Until things settle down around here, alleviating my boredom isn't a good motive to leave. Sorry.

topics.prompt: Uh... it beats sitting around here all day, doesn't it?

responses.text: All right. Let's not waste any time. {a bit of enthusiasm} There are people out there to help, things to learn. Maybe not in that order, but let's get to it.
I'm not sure why you thought a Follower would want to help Caesar after all of the misery he's visited on us and the people we try to help.
Well, good luck to you in your future endeavors, assuming they don't involve Caesar.

topics.prompt: Oh, well... in that case, never mind.

responses.text: Overt flirtation will get you everywhere, you know.
On a slightly more serious note, if you're interested in helping out with the troubles plaguing Freeside, I can come with you.
Just don't do anything obnoxious, like trying to help Caesar's Legion, and we should be fine. Understood?

topics.prompt: I need a good-looking doctor to help take care of me in the big, bad wasteland.

responses.text: Plasma rifles. They were intended to replace the P94 plasma caster.
There was some corporate espionage going on between Poseidon Energy's Project SEMELE and whatever was going on here.
REPCONN went through some rough times. When their rocket business was shaky, Mr. House purchased the company.

Another one of Poseidon Energy's many secret weapons projects. Before the Great War. It didn't go anywhere.
That's how REPCONN got their shot. So to speak.
Me, specifically? No. I'm sure Julie Farkas does, though. Lab coat, pointy hair. Answers to the name "Julie Farkas," strangely enough.

Here's my proposition. If you want to work together to help the people around here, I'll lend a hand. {on the other hand} If you start acting like a crazy waster...

topics.prompt: Would you like to come with me? I could use someone skilled in medicine.

responses.text: See you around.
Well {emph} I don't. I'm sure there were a few people turning a blind eye, but can you blame them?
NCR's sharecropper farms had all of the water. The nearest fresh source is the lake, and that's a bit of a hike.

topics.prompt: Right. "The Followers don't endorse his actions," and all that.

responses.text: I do say so. The Followers aren't a military organization. If anyone knew what he was up to, they weren't talking.

topics.prompt: If you say so. I'm not arguing.

responses.text: Of course.

topics.prompt: I'm sorry. I didn't realize it would end like this.

responses.text: {irritated} I guess that means you don't have to apologize to all of the people in Westside you just screwed over.

In case I'm not laying down enough sarcasm, you just screwed up the lives of a bunch of struggling people.

topics.prompt: Anderson killed White. He deserved to pay for what he did.

responses.text: Huh. {trying to think of a plausible lie} Good question. Must have been in a book.

topics.prompt: What do you know about them?

responses.text: Look, the Followers have had enough of a role in the misery that this area has had to endure.

Certainly.
The last time we discussed this, you didn't exactly wow me with your pitch. What have you got for me this time?

topics.prompt: Would you reconsider my offer to travel with me? I could really use your help.

responses.text: I'm really very boring. You'd get better stories out of a Freeside junkie.
You're helping the Legion, a slaving army that will almost certainly kill and enslave the majority of people in New Vegas.
What? Did you expect me to applaud your efforts to support a deranged warlord?
Caesar is bad. You are bad for helping him. Please stop.
I have to say I don't understand where you're going with Mr. House. The man's been manipulating the locals for as long as anyone can remember.
If you help him kick the NCR and Legion out, he's going to keep right on doing it. The people in Freeside will be just as bad off as they ever were.
If you can find a way to push Mr. House out of the picture as well, I think everyone will be better off.
Helping the NCR is better than helping Mr. House, but I don't think it's the best solution for the people in New Vegas.
If the NCR can take full control of Freeside and the Strip, it's going to get worse before it gets better.

I think you're on the right track.
The only way to ensure relative safety and independence for the people of New Vegas is to prevent others from taking control of the region.
That means no NCR, no Mr. House, and no Legion.

topics.prompt: What's your opinion on the current situation?

responses.text: {sickened} That's one way to look at it.

topics.prompt: They profit from crime, now I profit, too.

responses.text: {joking} I thought my charm could win you over, but I guess it wasn't meant to be. Are you sure you want me to go?

I've been around a few unsettling places in my life, but that place takes the cake.
Anyway, if you need me, you know where to find me.
{sighing} Back to the tomb, I suppose.
{drifting off} If you need me, et cetera.
You have quite the menagerie at your disposal. If you can get the posse down to "small gang" size, I'll happily go with you.
As the old saying goes, two's company, but three's a small army. Okay, I'm paraphrasing a bit, but you get the idea.
A courier, a doctor, and cybernetic dog. After we deal with this whole "imminent conquest of New Vegas" problem we should open an act at the Tops.

Well, there are worse things happening in the world, right?
After spending thirty years of my life hiding my association with the Enclave, I'd {emph} love to stroll the wasteland with a twitchy Eyebot.
Thanks for asking. I appreciate it. I do.
Back in your good graces again? I knew you'd see the light.

topics.prompt: I'd like you to come with me.

responses.text: It just seems a little twitchy. Some of these robots, you look at them the wrong way, don't screw in a vacuum tube right...
The next thing you know you're a pile of ash on the floor and someone's stepping out of a vertibird to sweep your remains into a Nuka-Cola bottle.
